A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IoUCert and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding methods, proofs, and experiments can be matched despite appendix renumbering and added material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original training accuracies, verification outcomes and runtimes, and pooling ablations for SSD and YOLO models.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain original experiments and add training and verification results for YOLOv3-tiny on COCO single-object crops.

M1.justification: The core verification framework is retained, but appendix pseudocode receives operational corrections. Algorithm 2 changes minimum/maximum initialization from 0/1 to 1/0 and updates both extrema independently. Algorithm 3 corrects the propagation input and candidate-threshold variable. These change the stated procedure without establishing that the implementation or retained experiments changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds COCO training and evaluation at 128×128 alongside the retained LARD and Pascal VOC coverage. COCO is converted into single-object crops, excluding inseparable overlapping objects. This substantially broadens the evaluated data while retaining the single-object task.

E2.justification: Cohen et al. remains the evaluated IoU-bounding comparator in Table 2 and v1 Table 7/v3 Table 8. The pooling ablation retains the same AvgPool and MaxPool variants. Newly discussed methods such as ATSS, PAA, and OTA are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The added COCO experiment introduces cropping and overlap-exclusion procedures and a 128×128 model configuration trained for 2000 epochs with learning rate 0.01 and weight decay 0.0005. The existing 50-image sampling design, metrics, perturbation budgets, and retained benchmark settings remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 extends the existing motion-blur angle analysis to COCO, adding evidence at 45, 90, and 135 degrees and showing a sharper robustness decline at large perturbation budgets. The pooling ablation, bound-tightness analysis, and complete-verification runtime analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report verification counts and mean runtimes without repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added COCO results use the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 3 and 6 add COCO verification counts and runtimes across brightness, contrast, and four motion-blur angles. Table 5 adds COCO mAP0.5 of 44.99% and mAP0.5:0.95 of 26.56%. These are new-setting results, not same-setting gains. Retained results largely agree; one LARD Table 3 runtime changes from 107.78 to 107.77 seconds.

T1.justification: v3 corrects boundary indices in Section 4.2, repairs the candidate-exclusion proof argument, and fixes the LeakyReLU restatement and positive-input area derivation in Appendix G. The elementary injective-composition proof is replaced by a citation. Appendix H adds a conditional NMS certification sketch; the central theorems and conclusions remain.

C1.justification: Both versions claim optimal IoU bounds, coordinate-transformed verification of single-object SSD/YOLO variants, and optimal LeakyReLU relaxations. v3 makes the tractable-variant and future end-to-end scope more explicit, but v1 already restricted the work to single-object localisation. COCO adds supporting evidence without replacing these central claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 and Appendix H substantially develop applicability and limitations: invertible decoding, independence from training-time label assignment, potential use in RPN and anchor-free heads, and obstacles involving attention and proposal processing. They explain the quadratic pairwise-overlap burden and ambiguous suppression decisions for NMS. v3 also adds dataset and resolution interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 supplies COCO-specific preprocessing rules, minimum object size, six anchor shapes, the 8,852,366-parameter model size, training hyperparameters, and validation-set evaluation information. Existing LARD implementation details, hardware disclosures, and repository references are retained.

R1.justification: New references include COCO, ATSS, PAA, OTA, and Hammack's proof textbook. The cited Xu work for LeakyReLU support changes to a different paper, while Kern et al. and YOLOv6 references disappear. Positioning expands to distinguish training-time assignment from inference verification, while the main comparison with prior verifiers remains.

P1.justification: v3 streamlines selected abstract, background, benchmark, and conclusion paragraphs, clarifies candidate enumeration, and brings pooling discussion into the main narrative. It adds dedicated scope sections and copyedits proofs and author information. The central section sequence and most technical exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the geometric candidate-set Figure 3 and substantially redesigns the verification tables with larger text, abbreviated R/NR/T columns, and explicit dataset/resolution groups. The training table is split into Tables 4–5, captions move above tables, and several existing displays are relocated. These changes materially alter presentation and legibility.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs concrete pseudocode and derivation inconsistencies, broadens empirical support through COCO crops, and makes applicability and NMS limitations easier to assess. The clearer tables and geometric illustration also help. These are incremental gains over an already developed method and evaluation. The new explanation linking resolution-related robustness differences to looser bounds is not established by Table 3's fully resolved cases, but this limited interpretive weakness does not outweigh the improvements.
